R0083.title: Insufficient Employee Security Awareness
R0083.definition: Refers to the potential threat that security incidents may occur due to unsafe behaviors by employees in their daily work due to insufficient security awareness.
R0083.description: Scenarios may include employees falling victim to phishing attacks, using weak passwords, sharing account information, clicking on unknown links indiscriminately, failing to update patches in a timely manner, or having their accounts compromised through social engineering.
R0083.influence: Harms include theft of sensitive information, unauthorized access to company systems, data tampering, and malicious operations performed under stolen identities, posing potential threats to the company's confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

observables: Employee accounts show anomalous logins after phishing or social engineering, with sudden changes in source IP, device, or geography
Corporate mailboxes are reported with large volumes of weak or reused passwords, and credentials appear in leak databases
Employees click phishing links or download malicious attachments, with frequent EDR alerts on endpoints
Employees share accounts or click unknown links indiscriminately, and human factors account for a high share of incidents in weekly security reports

R0083-001.title: Employee Account Compromise
R0083-001.definition: The potential threat that accounts of internal employees may be obtained and misused by unauthorized individuals or malicious parties.
R0083-001.description: Common scenarios for employee account compromise include employees falling victim to phishing attacks, using weak passwords, sharing account information, or being manipulated through social engineering, resulting in account compromise. After obtaining the account, attackers commonly use it for unauthorized access to sensitive data, lateral movement, or as a pivot for further attacks; because the account itself carries legitimate permissions, traditional perimeter defenses struggle to detect it, posing a persistent threat to the organization's confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
R0083-001.influence: Harms include theft of sensitive information, unauthorized access to company systems, data tampering, and malicious operations performed under stolen identities, posing potential threats to the company's confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

observables: Employee account login source IPs, devices, or geographies deviate significantly from prior profiles
Compromised accounts anomalously access or download sensitive data beyond the user's responsibilities
Credential-stuffing or leaked-credential databases contain matches for this organization's employee account passwords
Compromised accounts are used for unauthorized operations or as pivot points for lateral movement

R0083-002.title: Social Engineering Risk
R0083-002.definition: The potential threat that attackers use social engineering techniques to fraudulently exploit employees' trust and social connections to obtain sensitive information, steal credentials, or carry out other malicious activities, typically through false identities, impersonated communications, and social engineering tactics. In recent years, AI technologies (such as deepfake voice and video) have been used to enhance the credibility and success rate of social deception.
R0083-002.description: Common employee social engineering scenarios include: identity impersonation (attackers posing as senior management, colleagues, customers, or other trusted entities via email, social media, or instant messaging to request sensitive information or specific tasks); impersonated communications (sending fake emails, messages, or documents to induce employees to click malicious links, download malicious attachments, or provide sensitive information); AI Deepfake Deception (attackers use AI voice cloning or video synthesis technology to impersonate company leaders or colleagues for phone or video scams, significantly increasing deception success rates); social media fraud (creating fake profiles mimicking colleagues or superiors to establish contact and extract sensitive information); and fake emergencies (posing as urgent situations to induce employees to provide sensitive information or perform unsafe operations without proper verification).
R0083-002.influence: Harms include but are not limited to: information leakage of sensitive data, credentials, or company secrets; network intrusion through unauthorized access; financial losses from fraudulent financial operations; and reputational damage from customer trust issues or broken business partnerships.

observables: Emails or messages impersonating leaders or colleagues request fund transfers, credentials, or sensitive operations
AI voice cloning or video synthesis impersonates executives in phone or video scams, with victims filing reports
Financial or transfer operations bypass established approval flows and are carried out unilaterally by employees under social-engineering pressure
Fake accounts impersonating company employees or executives appear on social platforms and contact customers or colleagues
